articles.title: Healthy food is still out of reach for students and young people
articles.author: Peoples Health Dispatch
articles.content_excerpt: Students in secondary schools across England remain reliant on unhealthy food amid ongoing commercialization, weak accountability, and inaccessible prices. A recent report by the network Bite Back examines how these intersecting factors are affecting children’s nutrition, calling on the government to revise existing standards and ensure students can access real, nutritious food. Read more: Ultra-processed food dominates child nutrition in the UK The report found that a significant number of secondary school students still opt for “grab-and-go” items over full school meals. These predominantly carbohydrate-based options, such as pastries and chips, mostly fall short of existing nutritional standards. articles.title: ‘You won, Mr. President’: Press freedom under attack in Ecuador
articles.author: BreakThrough News
articles.content_excerpt: A few days ago, one of Ecuador’s most widely followed journalists, Gisella Bayona, announced that she would quit journalism due to pressure from the administration, led by right-wing President Daniel Noboa. “In recent hours, a pro-government media outlet has published serious accusations against me and my husband, attempting to link my questions about the lack of medicines in hospitals to personal interests.” Bayona was referring to the investigations she had conducted regarding the severe and chronic shortage of medicines and medical supplies in the public health system that has plagued the country for several years. Noboa has repeatedly promised to resolve this problem, but so far there has been no solution, while the number of deaths due to a lack of public health care continues to rise
